title: State PCS Exam Guide: Complete Strategy for State Civil Services
summary: Master state-level civil service examinations (UPPSC, BPSC, MPPSC, MPSC, RPSC) for SDM, DSP, and Naib Tehsildar posts with dedicated state GK guidance.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

State Public Service Commissions (such as UPPSC, BPSC, MPPSC, MPSC, RPSC, TNPSC, and WBPSC) conduct State Combined Civil Services Examinations to recruit Class-I and Class-II administrative officers for key provincial roles. These posts include Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), Block Development Officer (BDO), Commercial Tax Officer (CTO), and Naib Tehsildar. State PCS offers grassroots administrative authority and influential governance opportunities within the state.

## Eligibility Criteria

| Parameter | Requirements |
|---|---|
| **Educational Qualification** | Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognized University or equivalent qualification recognized by the state/central government. Specific degrees (Law for Assistant Prosecuting Officer, Commerce for Accounts Officer) required for technical posts. |
| **Domicile / State Residence** | Candidates from any Indian state are eligible to apply under the General/Unreserved category. Reserved category benefits (SC, ST, OBC, EWS, Women) are strictly reserved for permanent domicile holders of the recruiting state. |
| **State Language Competence** | High proficiency in the official language of the state (reading, writing, speaking) is required. Many states have mandatory qualifying language papers in Mains. |
| **Physical Fitness** | Specific minimum height and chest measurements apply for uniformed executive roles like DSP and District Jail Superintendent. |

## Age Limit & State-Level Relaxations

| Category | Standard Age Range | Upper Age Relaxation |
|---|---|---|
| **General (UR)** | 21 - 40 Years (21 - 37 in Bihar; 21 - 38 in Maharashtra) | Nil (0 Years) |
| **State Domicile OBC** | 21 - 40 Years | 3 to 5 Years upper age relaxation |
| **State Domicile SC / ST** | 21 - 40 Years | 5 Years upper age relaxation |
| **PwBD (State Domicile)** | 21 - 40 Years | Up to 15 Years upper age relaxation |
| **State Female Candidates** | 21 - 40 Years | Additional 3 to 5 years relaxation in states like MP, Bihar, Rajasthan |
| **State Government Employees** | 21 - 40 Years | Up to 5 Years relaxation for permanent civil staff |

## Common Examination Architecture

| Stage | Paper / Focus Area | Structure & Marks | Qualifying / Merit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Preliminary Stage** | GS Paper I (General Studies + State GK) | 150-200 Questions (150-200 Marks) | Decides cut-off for Mains (1/3rd Negative Marking) |
| **Prelims CSAT** | GS Paper II (Aptitude, Interpersonal Skills, Hindi/English) | 100 Questions (200 Marks) | Mandatory Qualifying (33% minimum) |
| **Mains Examination** | General Hindi / General English / Essay | Descriptive (100 - 150 Marks each) | Counted in Final Merit ranking |
| **Mains GS Papers** | General Studies I, II, III, IV, plus Dedicated State GS Papers | Descriptive 8-12 mark questions | Primary deciding factor for service allocation |
| **Personality Test (Interview)** | Assessment of leadership, state issue awareness & character | 100 - 175 Marks | Added to Mains score for final merit list |

## Physical Standards for Uniformed Posts (DSP / Excise Inspector)

| Parameter | Male Candidates | Female Candidates |
|---|---|---|
| **Height (UR / OBC)** | 165 cm - 168 cm | 152 cm - 155 cm |
| **Height (ST Category)**| 160 cm - 162 cm | 147 cm - 150 cm |
| **Chest (Unexpanded)** | Minimum 84 cm (with 5 cm expansion) | Not Applicable |
| **Chest (Expanded)** | Minimum 89 cm | Not Applicable |
| **Eye Sight** | 6/6 without glasses, normal color vision | 6/6 without glasses, normal color vision |

## Proven State PCS Preparation Roadmap

| Phase | Action Plan & State-Specific Strategy |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Master State-Specific GK & History** | Read comprehensive state handbooks covering the state's geography, tribal history, rivers, mineral resources, folklore, art and culture, state budget, and agricultural schemes. State GK now contributes 25-35% in Prelims and entire dedicated Mains papers in UPPSC, BPSC, and MPPSC. |
| **Phase 2: Standard National GS Curriculum** | Cover national History (Modern India focus), Indian Polity (articles and amendments), Physical and Indian Geography, and Economic Survey. |
| **Phase 3: Answer Writing for Mains** | Practice writing concise 125-word and 200-word descriptive answers within 7 minutes. Incorporate state maps, diagrams, government scheme names, and data points. |
| **Phase 4: Current Affairs of the State & Mock Tests** | Study 12 months of state-specific current affairs magazines. Solve 30 state Prelims test series papers to master factual and assertion-reasoning question formats. |

State PCS examinations reward applicants with thorough mastery of state folklore, geography, and local governance initiatives. Complement your national GS studies with regular state newspaper reading to secure a top rank.
